text: The book gives the general-relativistic deflection of a light ray grazing the Sun as about 1.75″. How does this compare with the value from the equivalence-principle / 'Newtonian falling photon' argument alone?
choices: It is half the Newtonian value
It is exactly twice the Newtonian value of about 0.875″
It is about ten times the Newtonian value
explanation: The GR result δφ = 4GM/(bc²) = 1.749″ is exactly twice the 'Newtonian'/EP-only prediction of 0.875″. Eddington's 1919 eclipse expedition measured about 1.75″, confirming the full GR value and ruling out the half-value. The extra factor of two comes from the curvature of space, which the naive falling-photon argument omits.
